lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Darnell, it's Yolanda. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, it went really well, I actually did it 3 times.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I told my family I'm done eating at 8. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My health is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is coffee with milk the first thing you have?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're already doing things to make it easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 8. Maybe 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 3 out of 3 days, the hard part was the hunger at night, and next week you're going to finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Darnell. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Gave dinner-timing advice right after participant voiced barrier (late dinners) without asking permission.
Repeated the exact permission question from line 14 after participant had already said yes; sign of not tracking the conversation.
Verbatim repeat of line 23 advice; pushes the same suggestion despite participant sustain talk.
Directive 'Once you decide something, you follow through' pressures commitment rather than exploring ambivalence.
Sustain talk about late dinners repeated and not explored; missed chance for complex reflection on the barrier.

score.summary: Darnell showed strong change talk, reporting three successful fasts, a concrete five-night goal, and a confidence of 8 to 9. The coach used good open questions and a clear summary, but repeated advice verbatim (lines 23 and 36) and repeated a permission question already answered (line 34), which undercut partnership.
strengths: Line 52 and 56: open questions elicited a concrete goal and anticipated barrier (hunger at night).
Line 58: clear summary with check for missed items, supporting collaboration.
Line 12 and 46: complex reflections captured Darnell's ambivalence and deeper motivation about family.
coaching_tips: Line 36 repeats line 23 verbatim; after sustain talk (line 33), reflect the barrier first and ask permission before offering advice again.
Line 34 re-asks permission already given at line 15; track the conversation so you do not repeat questions.
Line 40 ('Once you decide something, you follow through') pressures commitment; replace with a reflection such as 'You're still weighing how this fits your evenings.'
Line 29 and 33: explore the late-dinner barrier with an open question (e.g., 'What would make an earlier dinner workable?') rather than moving on.
Line 27 'Maybe' signals ambivalence; a complex reflection there could have deepened change talk.
